disclaimer: Authored simulation parameters are game-model inputs, not real-world weapon-effect predictions.

directionFrame.rule: Use the target-local frame at impact time; target rotation changes world-to-local direction.

pipeline: Intersect the event with current geometry and occlusion; resolve the first contacted surface and ordered layers behind it.
Evaluate penetration, deformation, transmitted load, heat, severed connections and local shock using authored model parameters.
Apply effects to physically exposed or connected parts, respecting barriers, isolation and compartment boundaries.
Evaluate secondary events only when an actual source and trigger exist: fire, pressure loss, fluid release, electrical fault, thermal damage, structural collapse or hazardous payload event.
Update only affected parts, neighbors, compartments and hazard events; preserve the causal chain in persistent history.
Record detached debris, surviving equipment, repair work, salvage condition and uncertainty.

rules: A weak point is a physical location or interface, not a magic damage multiplier.
A propulsion mount may be vulnerable because its location, protection, load path and connections make it vulnerable.
A damaged mount can impair thrust alignment without immediately destroying the engine; later operation may worsen the fault.
Prior impacts change geometry and condition, so later events must resolve against updated state.

survival.rule: Destroying a parent assembly does not automatically destroy each child. Evaluate each part from local exposure, support, barriers, heat, shock and subsequent collapse.

cascade.rule: Each secondary event has an identifiable trigger, transfer path, affected parts, source of energy/load/material, onset, termination or containment reason, and resulting work items.
stopConditions: remaining work deferred without erasing it
rules: Criticality describes consequences; it does not itself cause an explosion.
The same hit can produce different outcomes based on configuration, maintenance, operating state, orientation, load and previous damage.
Do not substitute one universal explosion outcome for the actual sequence of affected components and available energy.

performance.authoring: Precompute static geometry, face layers, part adjacency, occlusion and candidate transfer neighborhoods for each approved configuration.
performance.runtime: Resolve each event against current configuration and condition, then update only the affected neighborhood.
performance.persistence: Persist authoritative event and part state; cached tables are never the source of truth.
performance.determinism: Use event-keyed deterministic variation, never frame order or a global mutable random stream.
fidelity: tactical: part-level effects and local cascades
inspection: individual condition, debris and salvage
performance.optimization: Precompute candidate hit regions and transfer paths, not a universal outcome. Angle, configuration, prior damage, active systems and containment change the result.

steps: event intersects exposed mount or thrust-frame region
mount deforms according to local state
sensors and watch may detect vibration or thrust asymmetry
shutdown may limit further damage; continued operation may worsen it
repair requires isolation, support, inspection and alignment
scenarios.lesson: A precise hit creates a physical fault path, not an instant vehicle-delete event.

steps: local fault creates an ignition source
spread follows available fuel, oxygen, heat and connected spaces
doors, suppression, ventilation and crew response alter spread
heat and smoke affect nearby systems
suppression leaves inspection and contamination work
scenarios.lesson: Secondary damage depends on local conditions and response.

steps: large pieces separate at damaged joints
some enclosed modules survive while exposed components do not
debris moves according to local environment
recovery teams secure, inspect and catalog parts
accepted salvage returns to inventory with provenance
scenarios.lesson: The wreck persists as material, intelligence, hazards and history.
